paper.title: UAV-VLRR: Vision-Language Informed NMPC for Rapid Response in UAV Search and Rescue
paper.central_claim: Integrating vision-language mission interpretation with onboard point-to-point obstacle-avoiding NMPC enables faster and safe UAV search-and-rescue response, averaging 33.75% faster than an off-the-shelf autopilot and 54.6% faster than a human pilot.

evidence.locator: III-A Vision-Language Integration; fixed text line 15
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o serves as the LLM agent, responsible for extracting goal objects, specifically “target points” and “obstacles”.
evidence.support_explanation: Frozen-model semantic extraction upstream of geometric control, not controller learning.

evidence.locator: III-A coordinate conversion; fixed text line 15
evidence.quote: Specifically, the real-world coordinates are computed based on the camera’s height and field-of-view (FoV) parameters.
evidence.support_explanation: Coordinates assume camera metadata and approximately planar aerial geometry, not calibrated per-pixel metric depth.

evidence.quote: The control problem is iteratively solved in real time onboard the drone using CasADi [ 21 ] .
evidence.support_explanation: Numerical dynamics-constrained optimization owns low-level execution.

evidence.locator: IV Experimental Setup; fixed text line 18
evidence.quote: There were two different scenarios in which all the three experiments were conducted:
evidence.support_explanation: Only two arena layouts, each compared with autopilot and human; no independent deployment set described.

evidence.locator: IV timing protocol; fixed text line 18
evidence.quote: For the UAV-VLRR framework, the timing started as soon as the code was launched, while for the human pilot, the timing started as soon as the image was shown.
evidence.support_explanation: Mission-time endpoint has a start convention, but human and autonomous preparation are not fully matched.

evidence.locator: V-A Tables I-II validation; fixed text line 21
evidence.quote: For this analysis, an identification was considered accurate if the detected point was within a 25 cm radius of the actual object.
evidence.support_explanation: Object localization is checked against Vicon, but tolerance is not an audited mission-success verifier.

evidence.locator: V-B Table III; fixed text line 21
evidence.quote: TABLE III : Flight Results Exp 1 Exp 2 Exp 3 Time Taken for Scene 1 (s) 28 40 57 Time Taken for Scene 2 (s) 30 48 72
evidence.support_explanation: Supports descriptive mission-time arithmetic on two scenes, not a success-rate/general-safety estimate.

evidence.locator: VII Future Work; fixed text line 27
evidence.quote: Another important direction is the integration of dynamic environmental factors, such as moving obstacles, to improve the system’s relevance and robustness in real-world conditions.
evidence.support_explanation: Dynamic-disaster robustness remains future work, restricting general SAR claims.
